Hideko was interested to see if there was a relationship between what people earn and the age which they left education or training. She says her data supports the conclusion that more education causes people to earn a lower hourly rate of pay. Give one reason why Hideko’s conclusion might not be valid.
“Respondents who left education later would have significantly less work experience than those who left education earlier. This could be the cause of the reduced income shown in her results.”

transcription.tex: Question 5

The table shows the daily maximum relative humidity, h (%), and the daily mean visibility, v decametres (Dm), in Heathrow for the first two weeks in September 2015, from the large data set.\par $\begin{array}{l|ccccccc}h&94&95&92&80&97&94&93\\\hline v&2600&2900&3900&4300&2800&2400&2700\end{array}$\par $\begin{array}{l|ccccccc}h&90&87&95&93&92&91&98\\\hline v&3500&3000&2200&2200&3300&2800&2200\end{array}$\par The equation of the regression line of v on h is \(v=12700-106h\). \par (a) Give an interpretation of the value of the gradient of the regression line. \par (b) Use your knowledge of the large data set to explain whether there is likely to be a causal relationship between humidity and visibility. \par (c) Give reasons why it would not be reliable to use this regression equation to predict: (i) the mean visibility on a day with 100% humidity (ii) the humidity on a day with visibility of 3000 dm. \par (d) State two ways in which better use could be made of the large data set to produce a model describing the relationship between humidity and visibility.
(a) For each percentage-point increase in humidity, predicted mean visibility falls by 106 decametres.
(b) High humidity (above 95%) can cause mist and fog, reducing visibility. A causal link is plausible.
(c) (i) 100% is outside the observed range, so the prediction is an extrapolation.\par (ii) This line predicts visibility from humidity. Predicting humidity requires the regression of h on v.
(d) Randomly sample throughout September and analyse the whole month. Increase the sample size using several months between May and October.

Question 6

James placed different masses (\(m\)) on a spring and measured the resulting length of the spring (\(s\)) in centimetres. The smallest mass was 20 g and the largest mass was 100 g. He found the equation of the regression line of \(s\) on \(m\) to be \(s=44+0.2m\).\par (a) Interpret the values 44 and 0.2 in this context.\par (b) Explain why it would not be sensible to use the regression equation to work out: \par (i) the value of \(s\) when \(m=150\) \par (ii) the value of \(m\) when \(s=60\).
(a) With no mass attached, the predicted length is 44 cm. Adding 1 g increases predicted length by 0.2 cm.
(b) (i) $m=150$ is outside the data range, so this is extrapolation.\par (ii) This line predicts $s$ from $m$. To predict $m$ from $s$, use the regression of $m$ on $s$.
